original_test_intent: Verify every SMBIOS Type 28 Temperature Probe structure, its identity/location/status and all applicable limit, resolution, tolerance, accuracy and nominal-temperature fields against the approved platform specification.
original_method: Collect complete raw Type 28 structures through protected read-only OS access, retain SUT/SMBIOS/parser identity, decode every handle and numeric/sentinel field, compare to the expected thermal-probe matrix and label any live sensor readback as supplemental only.
manual_activity: The platform/thermal owner supplies the expected temperature-probe inventory, fields, units and sentinel rules; an operator verifies target identity and protected access while automation performs the comparison.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board, BIOS and SMBIOS version
Expected Type 28 handle count, descriptions and locations
Expected status, maximum/minimum, resolution, tolerance, accuracy, OEM and nominal values
Documented temperature units, signedness/precision, rounding and Unknown/not-provided sentinels
Supported dmidecode/parser version and raw-field mapping
Protected credential/host verification, redaction and evidence storage
safety_requirements: Keep collection read-only; do not alter fan curves, thermal thresholds, workload, BIOS or BMC policy
Do not clear logs before relevant baseline evidence is retained
Never put passwords on the command line or disable host-key verification
Capture complete raw stdout/stderr and exit status; no heading-only grep verdict
Preserve raw numeric encodings before temperature conversion or rounding
Do not treat SMBIOS nominal/limit metadata as a live temperature measurement
Stop on malformed, unit-ambiguous or sentinel-ambiguous data and require owner interpretation
agent_execution_scope: Validate target and expected Type 28 probe matrix
Collect complete raw `dmidecode --type 28` through protected access
Parse every handle, location, status and numeric/optional field
Apply only documented temperature unit, precision and sentinel transformations
Optionally correlate separately labelled read-only BMC/OS temperature telemetry
Report comparison and no-mutation audit without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve probe inventory, expected values, units and tolerances
Resolve Unknown, OEM, not-provided or absent entries
Define whether supplemental live thermal correlation is required
Review evidence and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Type 28 selector matches the source, but grep hides probe and numeric fields, while sshpass plus disabled host checking exposes credentials and weakens target identity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use protected authenticated access to run unfiltered `dmidecode --type 28`, retaining complete stdout/stderr, exit status, target identity, parser version and raw numeric values before conversion.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Type 28 scope, SPEC comparison, private script and 10/10-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: TYPE28 PROBE MATRIX AND TEMPERATURE SEMANTICS REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a handle-indexed table of every temperature probe, decode status and raw limit/resolution/tolerance/accuracy/nominal fields with explicit units and sentinels, then compare to SPEC before optional live-sensor correlation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds complete multi-probe parsing, raw-to-temperature traceability, secure target binding and inventory-versus-live evidence separation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A decoder heading cannot reveal missing probes, swapped locations, wrong thresholds or impossible minimum/maximum relationships.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SMBIOS values may be design metadata and can differ from live telemetry by purpose and update cadence; no thermal stimulus or remediation is authorized.

project_override_considerations: If the Project expects zero Type 28 entries, that absence must be explicit. Live BMC or OS temperatures may corroborate sensor identity but cannot replace SMBIOS structure coverage.
expected_evidence: SUT/BIOS/SMBIOS/parser identity, timestamp and approved Type 28 matrix
Complete raw Type 28 stdout/stderr and exit status
Parsed handles, descriptions, locations, status and all numeric/optional fields
Raw-to-unit calculations, sentinel handling and field/invariant comparison
Separately labelled optional live thermal correlation plus no-mutation/security audit
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target SMBIOS Type 28 Temperature Probe information. Missing expected inventory and numeric semantics are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Type 28 collection and comparison are deterministic once the probe matrix, units and parser policy are supplied.

review_improvement: Retains the correct Type 28 read while adding all probe/numeric fields, raw-to-temperature traceability, protected identity and separation from live telemetry.
independent_technical_reasoning: A temperature-probe record is accepted by its handle-to-location mapping and coherent encoded limits/nominal value under the correct unit and sentinel rules. Live temperature answers current operating state, so it can corroborate identity but cannot prove the firmware inventory fields requested here.
